So, I've been wanting to write a novel for a god damn long time now. When I was a kid (Which technically am a kid still, but eh.) I thought of how awesome it would have been to see people reading books that I wrote, and enjoy the worlds I create through words on paper alone, and making stories and characters that people cared about. But, there's a reason why I put off writing novels, something I haven't been able to come to terms with, until recently in a sort of epiphany. And it is what I dub "The creators curse". (As a side note, I'm not to sure if this idea is floating around somewhere, or already has a name. But Ill just go with what I have.)

The reason why I want to make novels, is to write something that I would want to read. However, as an author of the novel, that is impossible. I already know what's going to happen, and I have the power to just change it if I so wish. Even though I am making the damn thing, I cannot experience my work like the viewer can. This applies to any creative medium, except for painting, and video game development. those are the only two things that I can come up with, that the creators curse does not apply to.

This totally bummed me out, for at least two and a half years minimum. Until, I realized a little something else. If no one makes any sort of medium, this simply does not exist. But then consumers will have nothing to read, watch, play, observe or enjoy. And if this is the case, then creativity might as well not exist.

So, I have finally decided that this is the day that I put my creativity to use, even if I cannot enjoy my own work, perhaps my possible future fans might. I just wanted to share this idea with all of you lovely people, thoughts?
Why I finally stopped procrastinating on writing a novel, and what I call "The Creators Curse"
